candidate.scope: The assigned MeRIP-Seq / m6A-seq / m6A-RIP row under RNA Modifications: one simplified, shared extraction → RNA fragmentation → antibody enrichment → reverse-transcription route ending at cDNA. The three printed names are retained as grouped targets, not asserted to be interchangeable aliases or identical complete protocols. For m6A-RIP the scope is the cited Batista sequencing application (m6A RIP-seq) within that broader label. The two left RNA/RBP context icons have no interconnecting arrow and do not create alternative preparative branches. The separately labeled miCLIP-m6A row below and cropped scTrio-seq DNA workflow above are neighboring entries with separate routes, not targets or branches of this card. No UV crosslinking, RT truncation, input-control split or downstream sequencing operation is drawn in the assigned row.

states.label: Methylated RNA in its biological context
features: The left of the assigned row labels Methylated RNA and RBP beside illustrative RNA/chromatin/protein contexts; these are the starting biological context, not additional reagents or operations.
The paired contextual illustrations are not connected as a before/after transformation or shown to feed separate routes.
In this m6A-labeled row, red marks on the purple RNA denote the targeted RNA methylation. No 5′/3′ end groups, adapters, barcodes or defined covalent RNA–protein attachment are specified.

operations.description: Recover RNA from the illustrated methylated-RNA/RBP biological context into an extracted RNA population, drawn as a continuous purple RNA strand retaining red modification marks.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the target-containing RNA into the preparation; the RBP/chromatin illustrations provide context and do not establish an RNA–protein interaction measurement or required covalent crosslink.

operations.label: Fractionate RNA
operations.description: Fragment the extracted RNA population into shorter RNA molecules. Both modification-marked and unmarked fragments are depicted; the methylation marks stay associated with the fragments that carry them.
operations.mechanism: The source caption is Fractionate RNA; the visible strand shortening is interpreted as fragmentation, consistent with the MeRIP-Seq primary paper. No specific fragmentation chemistry is assigned to the grouped methods.
operations.information_effect: Subsequent affinity selection retains fragment-scale sequence regions associated with methylation, rather than necessarily retaining complete parent transcripts.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate
operations.description: Use antibody binding to enrich modification-associated RNA from the previously fragmented population. Pink antibodies are shown binding red-marked fragments; the following panel retains red-marked RNA fragments for reverse transcription. Recovery is summarized within this immunoprecipitation block, without inventing an extra elution operation.
operations.mechanism: m6A-specific antibody affinity selection; the antibodies are selection reagents, not the molecules converted into the sequencing readout.
operations.information_effect: Introduces an enrichment association between the selected RNA fragment sequence and antibody recognition of the modification. This selection can include nonspecific material and does not identify the exact modified nucleotide within each fragment.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Reverse-transcribe the enriched RNA fragments into cDNA, represented by blue DNA lines at the cDNA endpoint. This local substrate has already undergone the fragmentation and immunoprecipitation shown upstream.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated synthesis of cDNA, at the broad level stated by the caption; the diagram does not specify primers, enzymes or library-construction internals.
operations.information_effect: Preserves selected RNA sequence in a DNA readout carrier. Downstream sequencing, described in text but not drawn as an operation here, supports locating antibody-enriched RNA regions. Enrichment reflects selection history, not direct copying of a methylation mark into a separately readable cDNA feature. Fragment-level peaks do not by themselves resolve individual methylated residues or absolute per-site modification stoichiometry. The primary papers use non-IP input comparisons to interpret enrichment; no input-control branch is drawn in this assigned row.
